title: SNAP, food banks and hunger, 18 days of posts

clusters.text: Middle Eastern-looking men load cart after cart of milk at Walmart at the start of every month and sometimes take all of it.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim is an anecdote from one X account (@mymomcare, Oct 2, 2026). The post gives no store, city or state, so nothing ties it to Texas, and no records or news reporting confirm it. The account's video shows carts of milk jugs. As [The Daily BS](https://thedailybs.com/2026/10/05/middle-eastern-looking-walmart-shoppers-load-cart-after-cart-with-milk-and-the-internet-has-plenty-of-theories/) noted, 
the video does not establish who the shoppers are, how they paid, where the milk was going or whether anything improper occurred.
 The "Middle Eastern-looking" label is the poster's own appearance-based guess, and replies in the thread supplying SNAP-resale explanations (
buying with SNAP cards and selling for cash at their stores
) are speculation. Those replies offer no evidence. A commenter in a repost's comments even says they see the same thing in Arizona with Hispanic shoppers. Real SNAP trafficking cases exist, such as [a Texas store owner sentenced for swapping benefits for cash](https://fraudoftheday.com/food-benefits-sold-for-cash/). NPR reports that [organized theft rings often time their purchases to the start of the month](https://www.wbhm.org/2026-10-14/theyre-stealing-fr

clusters.text: SNAP users spend $8 billion on DoorDash every year.
clusters.verdict_basis:
I found no record or reporting that SNAP users spend $8 billion a year on DoorDash. The "$8 billion" figure that does appear in SNAP coverage is the monthly total of all SNAP benefits. 
USDA warned that 40+ million beneficiaries would miss an estimated $8 billion in November benefits
, and another source says 
benefits average about $8 billion per month
. The claim may have confused that number with DoorDash. Total SNAP spending was 
$101.7 billion in FY 2025
. Total online SNAP redemptions across all retailers were 
$2.3 billion in the July–September 2023 quarter
, which is roughly $9 billion a year at that rate. An $8 billion share for DoorDash alone is therefore implausible, and no source supports it. DoorDash accepts EBT only for groceries and convenience orders, and 
SNAP recipients may only purchase SNAP-approved grocery items with their EBT cards
. DoorDash's own September 2026 report gives user growth, 
from nearly 3 million to more than 4.5 million consumers with SNAP/EBT cards added between June 2025 and June 2026
. It gives no dollar total of $8 billion.

clusters.text: SNAP spending on DoorDash is taxpayer abuse.
Arizona was hit hardest by SNAP cuts, with a 52% drop in recipients, about 400,000 people including children.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The Center on Budget and Policy Priorities (CBPP) SNAP Tracker says 
SNAP participation fell in Arizona by 52 percent from July 2025 to June 2026
. The same tracker says the decline is 46 percent through August 2026, using newer state data. USDA figures reported by Newsweek show 
Arizona recorded 465,659 fewer participants
 in June 2026 than a year earlier. The CBPP tracker's August figure is 
a drop of 416,924
, which fits "about 400,000". Arizona has the largest percentage decline in the country. Louisiana, the next largest in the Newsweek and CBPP data, 
fell about 21.5 percent
. Children are included: 
205,223 children are no longer receiving the benefit since July 2025, a 55% drop
, according to AZ Luminaria. The claim has two weaknesses:
- "Hardest hit" is true by percentage only. Georgia and Texas lost more people in absolute terms.
- The 52% figure and the "about 400,000" figure come from different periods. 52% of Arizona's July 2025 caseload is closer to 460,000 people. This is a minor imprecision.

The claim's wording also treats the drop as "cuts". ProPublica and Newsweek report that much of it came from

clusters.text: Rep. Juan Ciscomani voted for the Big Beautiful Bill, which cut SNAP.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Ciscomani, who represents Arizona's 6th District, not a Texas seat, did vote for the bill. 
The House passed it 215-214 on May 22, 2025, and Ciscomani voted with nearly all of his GOP colleagues
 (Tucson Sentinel). The AFL-CIO scorecard also records his May 22, 2025 "yes" vote on H.R. 1. 
Copper Courier reports that every Arizona Republican in Congress backed the final law
, but I did not find a roll-call record of his July 2025 final-passage vote. On the substance, 
the CBO estimated the law cuts federal SNAP spending by $186.7 billion over 10 years
 (AEI summarizing CBO). 
The CBO also estimated its work-requirement provisions would reduce SNAP participation by 2.4 million people in an average month
 (Brookings). The AEI piece notes that about 35% of the reduction comes from shifting costs to states, but it is still a cut to federal SNAP spending, so "cut SNAP" is a fair description. The wording is accurate. The Texas framing comes from the monitoring context, not from the claim itself.
